content.title: Tools and Techniques for Data-Driven Insights in Energy
content.cta: Scroll, tab or use your keyboard to move ahead

content.text:
This chapter explores the application of data science techniques and energy modelling tools to drive data-driven insights in the energy sector. It emphasizes the role of Exploratory Data Analysis in uncovering patterns, identifying anomalies, and validating data for further analysis, with a focus on leveraging AI to automate processes like data cleaning, clustering, and anomaly detection. The module also highlights the integration of remote sensing 💬️ and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for spatial analysis, enabling precise monitoring of environmental changes and optimization of renewable energy resources.

Energy modelling is presented as a critical tool for policy analysis, system planning, and scenario evaluation, supporting decision-making in areas such as renewable energy integration, load forecasting, and grid stability. Case studies, including poverty mapping in the Philippines and clean energy transition planning in Tanzania, illustrate the practical application of these tools in real-world contexts. The module underscores the importance of high-quality data and robust data management practices in enhancing the accuracy and reliability of energy models.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Data Science Techniques for Energy Analysis
lessons.description: This lesson explores data science techniques for energy analysis, covering exploratory data analysis (EDA) methods like anomaly detection and predictive modeling. It highlights AI-driven automation in data cleaning, remote sensing integration with GIS for renewable energy optimization, and the role of data visualization in translating complex energy data into actionable insights. The lesson emphasizes leveraging these tools to enhance decision-making and sustainability in the energy sector.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Energy Modelling Tools and Applications
lessons.description: This lesson explores energy modelling tools and their applications in analyzing and optimizing energy systems, covering descriptive, prescriptive, and predictive models for policy analysis, scenario planning, and load forecasting. It highlights renewable energy integration, grid stability, and the role of data value chains in ensuring accurate models to support sustainable energy decision-making and efficient resource management.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Applied Machine Learning in Energy Data
lessons.description: This section introduces the use of Machine Learning (ML) in energy policy, focusing on structured data, learning models, and ethical concerns. It covers key applications like energy forecasting and emissions profiling using tools such as Random Forests and clustering. Foundational concepts are linked to real-world use cases to support evidence-based policymaking. The lesson ends by addressing ethical risks and promoting best practices like Explainable AI and Privacy by Design.
